findings.title: IPv4-mapped IPv6 bypasses the BLOCKED_HOSTS metadata check
findings.problem: The new hunk normalizes IPv4-mapped IPv6 only against the four address-class predicates, not against BLOCKED_HOSTS. BLOCKED_HOSTS is compared at line 77 as a raw hostname string, so `http://[::ffff:100.100.100.200]:8989` (Alibaba metadata) never matches the string set, is not link-local/loopback/unspecified/multicast in either its IPv6 or its mapped IPv4 form, and is accepted. The same is true for any future numeric entry added to BLOCKED_HOSTS. `169.254.169.254` happens to survive only incidentally because its mapped form is link-local.
findings.fix_hint: inside the ipv4_mapped branch, also `if str(mapped) in BLOCKED_HOSTS: return (False, "Blocked hostname")` — or normalize the hostname to its mapped IPv4 form before the BLOCKED_HOSTS lookup at line 77
findings.why_it_matters: The function's stated purpose is blocking SSRF to cloud metadata endpoints; the mapped-IPv6 form defeats the string-based half of that defense while the new code closes only the predicate-based half.

findings.problem: validate_arr_url has two parallel SSRF layers that no longer agree on address normalization. Layer 1 (line 77) matches the raw hostname string against BLOCKED_HOSTS; layer 2 (lines 81-88) now normalizes IPv4-mapped IPv6 before applying property checks. Because normalization happens only inside layer 2, the IPv4-mapped form of a BLOCKED_HOSTS entry skips layer 1 entirely. Concretely: '169.254.169.254' and '::ffff:169.254.169.254' both get blocked, but only by luck -- the mapped form is caught by mapped.is_link_local, not by the denylist. The Alibaba entry has no such backstop: verified with the stdlib that ipaddress.ip_address('::ffff:100.100.100.200').ipv4_mapped is 100.100.100.200 with is_link_local/is_loopback/is_unspecified/is_multicast all False, so 'http://[::ffff:100.100.100.200]:7878' passes validation while 'http://100.100.100.200:7878' is rejected. 'metadata.google.internal'/'metadata.azure.com' are unaffected (not IPs). The architectural fix is to normalize the address once, up front, and run BOTH the denylist and the property checks against the normalized form -- rather than teaching only the second layer about mapped addresses. pending: confirm with the owner whether the Alibaba mapped-form gap is in scope for D-10 or is deliberately deferred; D-10's text scopes the mapped check to 'the same blocklist', which reads as the property checks it enumerates, not necessarily BLOCKED_HOSTS.

intent_doc_match.note: The doc authorizes the exact code shape shipped (59-RESEARCH.md lines 210-218 contain this diff nearly verbatim), so the implementation is faithful. The ambiguity is what 'the same blocklist' names: the property checks the doc enumerates, or BLOCKED_HOSTS as well. Under the narrow reading the diff is complete; under the broad reading the BLOCKED_HOSTS layer was left un-normalized. Not confident enough to call this an unauthorized deviation.

findings.title: IPv4-mapped IPv6 block is dead code — stdlib already normalizes these
findings.problem: Lines 84-88 are unreachable in every case they claim to handle. Python's ipaddress already delegates is_loopback / is_link_local / is_multicast / is_unspecified through the mapped IPv4 address for ::ffff: forms. Verified directly on this machine: ipaddress.ip_address('::ffff:127.0.0.1').is_loopback is True, '::ffff:169.254.169.254'.is_link_local is True, '::ffff:224.0.0.1'.is_multicast is True, '::ffff:0.0.0.0'.is_unspecified is True. All four are therefore already caught by line 82 and return before line 85 is evaluated. The four SHIELD-007 mapped-IPv6 tests in tests/test_validation.py (lines 94-110) pass identically with lines 84-88 deleted, so the test suite provides no evidence this block does anything. The multicast addition on line 82 is genuine and load-bearing — that half of the diff is real. This is not a correctness bug; the block is harmless. It is a maintenance hazard: it reads as the mechanism enforcing D-10, so a future reader will trust it as the mapped-address defense while the actual bypasses (see impact-002, impact-003) sit outside it untouched.
findings.fix_hint: Either drop lines 84-88 as redundant, or repurpose the mapped-address unwrap to do the thing the stdlib does NOT do for you — re-check the unwrapped IPv4 string against BLOCKED_HOSTS (see impact-002).
findings.why_it_matters: The block creates false confidence that IPv4-mapped SSRF is handled, while the one mapped-form gap that genuinely exists (BLOCKED_HOSTS bypass) is left open directly beside it.

findings.title: BLOCKED_HOSTS string match bypassed by IPv4-mapped IPv6 form of the same metadata IP
findings.problem: BLOCKED_HOSTS (line 18) is compared as a raw hostname string at line 77, before any IP normalization. The two metadata IPs in that set — 169.254.169.254 and 100.100.100.200 — are protected only by that string comparison plus whatever address-property check happens to also catch them. 169.254.169.254 is incidentally covered because is_link_local is True for both its plain and mapped form. 100.100.100.200 (Alibaba Cloud metadata) has NO address property set: not link-local, not loopback, not multicast, not unspecified. Verified on this machine: running the post-diff logic, hostname '100.100.100.200' returns blocked (string hit), but '::ffff:100.100.100.200' returns ALLOW — the string compare misses the bracketed IPv6 literal, and neither line 82 nor the new lines 85-88 flag it because none of the four properties are true for that address. So the new mapped-address block, which exists specifically to close mapped-form bypasses, walks right past the one mapped-form bypass that is actually reachable. The mapped form of any future non-property-based entry added to BLOCKED_HOSTS inherits the same hole.
